# Premium Static Front-End Website Master Checklist

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. -->

This system is for premium static front-end only websites built from HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
It excludes backend application code, paid builders, paid plugins, and proprietary lock-in.

## Governing Rules
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Each numbered demo site must keep its own transformation pack: theme, layout, partials, components, CSS, JS, assets, page-section style map, mobile, conversion, and cross-site difference report.
- [ ] Each numbered demo site must keep an inspiration audit before visual coding: 3 direct industry references, 2 adjacent references, 2 contrast references, and 1 interaction or UI pattern reference.
- [ ] Reference extraction must capture layout archetype, header, desktop navigation, mobile menu, footer, typography, colour/surface, hero, section rhythm, cards, forms, CTA flow, assets, image treatment, icon/illustration style, JS ideas, motion, mobile behaviour, and what must not be copied.
- [ ] Inspiration references may inform principles only; never copy code, copy, logos, images, brand assets, exact layouts, exact animations, or proprietary identity.
- [ ] No numbered demo site may be accepted as a recolour, font swap, copied partial set, repeated card grid, repeated footer, repeated hero, repeated JavaScript experience, repeated asset style, or repeated page rhythm.
- [ ] Each site must have a cross-site difference score of 4 or 5 before acceptance; scores 1, 2, and 3 fail.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Source Baselines
- [ ] Accessibility baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA from W3C WAI.
- [ ] Search baseline: Google Search Central guidance for crawlability, canonicals, structured data, localized pages, and local business data.
- [ ] Sitemap baseline: sitemaps.org XML Sitemap protocol.
- [ ] Performance baseline: Core Web Vitals with LCP, CLS, and INP, plus static-site asset budgets.
- [ ] Security baseline: OWASP guidance for Content Security Policy and common browser security headers.
- [ ] Privacy baseline: jurisdiction-specific legal review is mandatory when tracking, forms, marketing consent, cookies, or personal data are used.

## Completion Rules
- [ ] A checklist is complete only when every applicable item has evidence or a documented exception.
- [ ] Automated passes do not prove brand, content, legal, strategy, or conversion quality.
- [ ] Manual review is mandatory for accessibility, privacy, legal, content claims, and user journey quality.
- [ ] The deployed static output is the source of truth for launch acceptance.
- [ ] All fixes must preserve the static-only, free/open-source-friendly, portable architecture.
- [ ] Reports must include severity, issue code, affected page/file, evidence, fixability, and how-to-fix guidance for every automated finding.
- [ ] Human checklist failures must record expected standard, actual behavior, owner, target date, and residual risk.

## Comprehensive Coverage
- [ ] The generated checklist set covers UX, QA, SEO, analytics, tracking, accessibility, planning and strategy, hosting and infrastructure, front-end development, CMS/no-code export, security, DevOps/CI-CD, performance, monitoring and observability, legal/privacy/compliance, assets, content, conversion, multilingual, local SEO, static blog, portfolio/case studies, and static selling.
- [ ] Safe automated fixes are limited to mechanical source changes and generated support files; subjective, legal, brand, strategic, and full accessibility decisions require human evidence.
- [ ] Every future static site should run the Python audit/fix tool, publish JSON and Markdown reports, then complete the manual checklist evidence before launch.
- [ ] Every portfolio rebuild should run `python3 premium-static-site-system/tools/validate_transformation_packs.py` before visual acceptance.
